note: Exhaustive scan of the whole FlashSV1 client tree (126 files: every SWF + the 2/3.png core SWFs disguised with a .png extension). Every one of the 42 VN-char ABC constant-pool string literals found lives in just 3 files: 2.png (34), 3.png (5), DDT_Loading.swf (3) — confirm/cancel dialog defaults, a handful of avatar-skin tier / stat-bonus / achievement-title strings, the in-arena tutorial NPC dialogue, and the loading screen. ZERO vietnam/swf/*.swf UI chrome files (shop.swf, roomlist.swf, bagandinfo.swf, email.swf, invite.swf, consortion*.swf, auction.swf, hall.swf, calendar.swf, setting.swf, ...) contain ANY ABC string literal with Vietnamese characters. This empirically confirms research/i18n/ui-sweep.md "Not fixed" item 1: the large native/dynamic UI-chrome class (Mua, Giỏ hàng, Tìm, Bắt đầu, Tổ đội, Xóa, equip-slot names, stat labels, table headers, pagers, Nam/Nữ filters...) is NOT baked into any ABC constant pool anywhere in the client. Decompiling 2.png (tools/i18n/abc-strings scan + ffdec -export script, see tank.data.EquipType.as) shows why: these all go through ddt.manager.LanguageMgr.GetTranslation("<dotted.key>") at runtime, resolved from language.txt loaded over the network — only the dotted KEY strings (ASCII, no Vietnamese) live in the ABC pool, never the display value. The served pt-BR language.txt already has correct translations (e.g. tank.data.EquipType.head -> "Chapéu", verified serving with HTTP 200), yet affected labels still render Vietnamese in the live client — e.g. ddt.data.EquipType.PARTNAME (EquipType.as) is a `public static const Array` whose entries are LanguageMgr.GetTranslation(...) calls evaluated ONCE at class-initialization time. If that class initializer runs before LanguageMgr.setup() has parsed the (possibly still-loading or cached) language.txt, the array permanently bakes in whatever _dic held at that instant. This static-initializer-ordering theory is new evidence, not yet proven by tracing actual load order; it is the most concrete lead for a follow-up task and squarely a different, larger problem than an ABC string-literal patch (would need an AS3 source change + recompile, e.g. converting PARTNAME-style arrays to lazy getters, or guaranteeing LanguageMgr.setup() always completes before any class with such an array is first touched).
